name: Metropolis
editorial_article: "Metropolis" is a landmark instrumental electro-house track that captures the quintessential sound of the early 2010s EDM (Electronic Dance Music) boom. Released in 2012 as part of David Guetta's "Nothing but the Beat (Ultimate Edition)," the track stands as a definitive collaborative effort between the French house veteran David Guetta and the rapidly rising Dutch producer Nicky Romero. At a time when electronic dance music was becoming a dominant global pop force, "Metropolis" served as a quintessential festival anthem, characterized by its sharp, metallic synth leads, driving four-on-the-floor rhythm, and meticulous production polish.\n\nBuilding upon the energetic house foundations that defined Guetta’s massive crossover success during this era, the track emphasizes tension and release through its intricate layering and dynamic drops. While many of Guetta's compositions from this period leaned heavily on radio-friendly vocal features, "Metropolis" highlighted the producer's technical engagement with the instrumental roots of big room house. Nicky Romero’s involvement brought a percussive tightness and harmonic complexity that resonated with the burgeoning European festival scene. The track remains a nostalgic artifact of a specific era, representing the precise moment when DJ-driven electronic music solidified its grip on global mainstream stages, merging club aesthetics with grand, stadium-ready soundscapes. It persists as a popular example of the collaborative energy that characterized the mid-2010s mainstream house movement.
